title: The Second Episode About Gulab Rai

blocks.text: Dohra:
If somebody made an enquiry, When did Gulab Rai become a Guru?
Then one should answer this question, By writing the following reply to this query: (1)
lines: Then one should answer this question,
By writing the following reply to this query:

blocks.text: Chaupai:

When (the Mughal emperor) Bahadur Shah visited Sirhind, He made an enquiry after calling Sulkhan2 Masand: If there lived anyone from Guru Gobind Singh's dynasty, Then a meeting be arranged between him and the emperor. (2)
lines: When (the Mughal emperor) Bahadur Shah visited Sirhind,
He made an enquiry after calling Sulkhan2 Masand: If there lived anyone from Guru Gobind Singh's dynasty,
Then a meeting be arranged between him and the emperor.

blocks.text: (At this), Sulakhan Masand, after calling Gulab Rai, Arranged a meeting between the emperor and Gulab Rai. The person (Gulab Rai) who occupied (Tenth) Guru's seat of Nanak, The emperor (Bahadur Shah) addressed him as Ramdas3 . (3)
lines: (At this),
Sulakhan Masand, after calling Gulab Rai,
Arranged a meeting between the emperor and Gulab Rai.
The person (Gulab Rai) who occupied (Tenth) Guru's seat of Nanak,
The emperor (Bahadur Shah) addressed him as Ramdas3 .

blocks.text: Bahadur Shah had been addressing the Sikh Gurus as Divine Gurus, Since he became a sovereign with the grace of Guru Gobind Singh. So Sulkhan Masand also arranged a meeting between the two, As was the practice among Mughal emperors of paying courtesy calls. (4)
lines: Bahadur Shah had been addressing the Sikh Gurus as Divine Gurus,
Since he became a sovereign with the grace of Guru Gobind Singh.
So Sulkhan Masand also arranged a meeting between the two,
As was the practice among Mughal emperors of paying courtesy calls.

blocks.text: Both the Mughal emperor and the Sikh Guru used to stand up, And take a step forward to receive each other respectfully. While the Mughal emperor used to fold his hands out of reverence, The Sikh Guru used to clasp the emperor's folded hands. (5)
lines: Both the Mughal emperor and the Sikh Guru used to stand up,
And take a step forward to receive each other respectfully.
While the Mughal emperor used to fold his hands out of reverence,
The Sikh Guru used to clasp the emperor's folded hands.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Sikh Gurus used to enquire about the visiting emperor's well-being, Gulab Rai also enquired about visiting Bahadur Shah's well-being. After emperor's assurance of his being well with Guru's grace, Both separated and departed for their respective destinations. (6)
lines: As the Sikh Gurus used to enquire about the visiting emperor's well-being,
Gulab Rai also enquired about visiting Bahadur Shah's well-being.
After emperor's assurance of his being well with Guru's grace,
Both separated and departed for their respective destinations.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As had been the convention of exchanging courtesies between emperors and Gurus, Emperor Bahadur Shah and Gulab Rai meeting was given a same colouring. Since emperor Bahadur Shah had been Guru's devout follower, Sulkhan Masand accorded the same significance to Gulab Rai's meeting. (7)
lines: As had been the convention of exchanging courtesies between emperors and Gurus,
Emperor Bahadur Shah and Gulab Rai meeting was given a same colouring.
Since emperor Bahadur Shah had been Guru's devout follower,
Sulkhan Masand accorded the same significance to Gulab Rai's meeting.

blocks.text: Getting this stamp of approval Gulab Rai set up his own pontifical seat, And earned peoples' reverence due to a Guru for about two years. All these details were narrated to (the author) Rattan Singh, By a person who happened to be a grandson of Gulab Rai. (8)
lines: Getting this stamp of approval Gulab Rai set up his own pontifical seat,
And earned peoples' reverence due to a Guru for about two years.
All these details were narrated to (the author) Rattan Singh,
By a person who happened to be a grandson of Gulab Rai.

blocks.text: Bhai Hazuri was the name of the narrator of this episode, And the author had recorded this episode as narrated to him. Sulakhan Dass, being the follower of Bhai Hazuri at present, Is among the select visitors who kept on visiting the author. (9)
lines: Bhai Hazuri was the name of the narrator of this episode,
And the author had recorded this episode as narrated to him.
Sulakhan Dass, being the follower of Bhai Hazuri at present,
Is among the select visitors who kept on visiting the author.

blocks.text: Now listen further about the life history of Gulab Rai, And the way he is related the Guru's family line.
Sri Guru Hargobind Singh fathered five respectable sons, The first and second being Bhai Gurditta4 and Teg Bahadur5 . (10)
lines: Sri Guru Hargobind Singh fathered five respectable sons,
The first and second being Bhai Gurditta4 and Teg Bahadur5 .

blocks.text: Sortha:
While the third son was named Ani Rai6 , The fourth son was named Atal Rai7 . Their fifth brother being named Suraj Mai8 , Which takes the number of Guru's sons to five. (11)
lines: While the third son was named Ani Rai6 ,
The fourth son was named Atal Rai7 .
Their fifth brother being named Suraj Mai8 ,
Which takes the number of Guru's sons to five.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

There being no need to write about the first four sons, Suraj Mai's life line alone must be described further. Since two sons were born to Suraj Mai, One was named Gulab Rai, the other being Shyam Chand9 . (12)
lines: There being no need to write about the first four sons,
Suraj Mai's life line alone must be described further.
Since two sons were born to Suraj Mai,
One was named Gulab Rai, the other being Shyam Chand9 .

blocks.text: It is the whole life history of Gulab Rai, Which needs to be narrated as it prevailed at that time. Whatever is the life history of Shyam Chand. It need not be narrated in this episode. (13)
lines: It is the whole life history of Gulab Rai,
Which needs to be narrated as it prevailed at that time.
Whatever is the life history of Shyam Chand.
It need not be narrated in this episode.

blocks.text: Whatever would occur and prevail in future, That would be recorded with due care as required. Now listen to the life story of Gulab Rai, As life and destiny dealt with him. (14)
lines: Whatever would occur and prevail in future,
That would be recorded with due care as required.
Now listen to the life story of Gulab Rai,
As life and destiny dealt with him.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Gulab Rai, who was related to Sodhi lineage, Had given rise to a very extended family line. He begot a large number of sons and grandsons, And acquired wealth beyond any reckoning. (15)
lines: Gulab Rai, who was related to Sodhi lineage,
Had given rise to a very extended family line.
He begot a large number of sons and grandsons,
And acquired wealth beyond any reckoning.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

While Dalel Singh and Jodh Singh were two among his sons, There were other sons with many other different names. In case the author started recording their names, There will be no end to the volume of this present epic. (16)
lines: While Dalel Singh and Jodh Singh were two among his sons,
There were other sons with many other different names.
In case the author started recording their names,
There will be no end to the volume of this present epic.

blocks.text: It is believed that he begot eighteen members of his progeny, With some of them getting married others remaining celibate. Gulab Rai was puffed up with lot of vanity and arrogance, As his household overflowed with wealth and affluence. (17)
lines: It is believed that he begot eighteen members of his progeny,
With some of them getting married others remaining celibate.
Gulab Rai was puffed up with lot of vanity and arrogance,
As his household overflowed with wealth and affluence.

blocks.text: As he held congregations after he occupied the Guru's seat, Money and wealth poured in from all the four directions. Excess of wealth pushed him into acts of perversion, As he came under the influence of evil stars. (18)
lines: As he held congregations after he occupied the Guru's seat,
Money and wealth poured in from all the four directions.
Excess of wealth pushed him into acts of perversion,
As he came under the influence of evil stars.

blocks.text: Within a span of two years, he met his doomed end, And similar fate struck his (inordinately extended) family.
He reaped the harvest of his (evil) deeds, Which sums up the whole life history of Gulab Rai. (19)
lines: He reaped the harvest of his (evil) deeds,
Which sums up the whole life history of Gulab Rai.
